ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Cardiology Referral — Benny Leonard — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Establishing primary care at 50 after a referee's license examination found high blood pressure: exertional breathlessness and chest tightness while refereeing, an ECG showing left ventricular hypertrophy, cardiovascular risk, money worries and mood, and a cardiology consultation

text.paragraph: A 50-year-old professional boxing referee and boxing instructor with newly found stage 2 hypertension, left ventricular hypertrophy by voltage on the ECG, and two months of breathlessness and chest tightness late in long nights of refereeing in hot arenas. Please evaluate the symptoms and the hypertrophy, advise on his coronary and sudden cardiac death risk, and say whether and how he can keep refereeing. [S]
Urgency: Soon, within two weeks; he is refereeing only short undercards until seen. [S]

list.item: Are his exertional breathlessness and chest tightness ischemic, and what test do you advise?
Is the left ventricular hypertrophy from hypertension, or could it be hypertrophic cardiomyopathy or an athlete's heart?
What is his risk of sudden cardiac death, and does he need ambulatory monitoring or other testing?
Would a coronary calcium score help decide on a statin and aspirin, and what do you recommend?
Can he keep refereeing, which means hours of moving about the ring in hot arenas, and with what precautions?

text.paragraph: Former world lightweight champion; referees whole cards of six to eight bouts several nights a week and teaches boxing. For about two months, late in long cards in hot arenas, breathlessness and tightness across the chest when moving quickly, easing within a few minutes of rest; never at rest; no fainting, palpitations, orthopnea or ankle swelling. Found at his yearly license examination to have blood pressure 164/100 and 160/98 mmHg, untreated. ECG today: sinus rhythm, left ventricular hypertrophy by voltage (Sokolow-Lyon 38 mm, Cornell 24 mm) with mild lateral T-wave flattening, QTc 418 ms, no Q waves or pre-excitation. Laboratory tests today: creatinine 0.98 mg/dL, potassium 4.1 mmol/L, HbA1c 5.5%, TSH 1.9, urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 22 mg/g, total cholesterol 234, LDL 160, HDL 44 mg/dL, lipoprotein(a) 42 nmol/L. Never smoked; little alcohol. Family history not known. Started today on losartan 50 mg with hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg with home monitoring. Money is tight since he lost his savings years ago, and he is anxious about his license; please favor low-cost generic medicines [S]

list.item: Breathless and tight in the chest late in long nights in the ring, and told his blood pressure is high. [S]
He needs his refereeing work and is afraid of losing his license. [S]
Worry about money since losing his savings years ago, and about the cost of medicines. [S]

text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: Benjamin Leiner was born on April 7, 1896, in New York City, to Gershon Leiner, a tailor, and Minnie Leiner, Orthodox Jewish immigrants from Russia, and grew up on the Lower East Side of Manhattan. [D]

He began fighting professionally at about fifteen and took the name Benny Leonard to keep his boxing secret from his parents, because boxing was not thought a respectable living in their community. [D]
He won the world lightweight championship from Freddie Welsh on May 28, 1917, and held it until he retired as undefeated champion in January 1925, at his mother's wish. [D]

The son of Orthodox Jews, he never fought on a Jewish holiday and became a symbol of the acceptance of Jews in American life at a time of open antisemitism; the newspaper editor Arthur Brisbane wrote that he had done more to conquer anti-Semitism than a thousand textbooks. He later supported the Maccabiah Games. [D]
Retired, he had become wealthy; in his own words he was practically a millionaire, without a scratch. [D]

He lost most of his savings in the 1929 stock market crash and in October 1931, at 35, came back as a welterweight; he won about nineteen fights in a row before Jimmy McLarnin knocked him out in the sixth round in October 1932, and he retired for good. [D]
During the Second World War he served in the U.S. Maritime Service of the Merchant Marine, rising to lieutenant commander. [D]
He returned to boxing as a referee of professional bouts in New York and also taught boxing at City College of New York. [D]

list.item: Breathlessness and tightness across the chest on exertion for about two months, late in long nights of refereeing in hot arenas, easing within a few minutes of rest; never at rest; no fainting, palpitations, orthopnea or ankle swelling; cause under evaluation with a cardiology consultation: active, confirmed [S]

Stage 2 hypertension found at a yearly fitness examination for his referee's license (164/100 and 160/98 mmHg), with left ventricular hypertrophy by voltage on the ECG; untreated; home readings to follow: active, confirmed [S]
Hypercholesterolemia: LDL 160 mg/dL, HDL 44 mg/dL, lipoprotein(a) not raised; no diabetes: active, confirmed [S]

High blood pressure: home monitoring with a validated upper-arm cuff, twice a day, with readings sent in weekly; single-pill losartan 50 mg with hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg from today, chosen as two first-line drugs for stage 2 hypertension and a low-cost generic; basic metabolic panel in two weeks; target below 130/80 mmHg; less salt (no more than 1,500 to 2,300 mg a day), the DASH pattern, and regular walking. Guideline: 2025 AHA/ACC/AANP/AAPA/ABC/ACCP/ACPM/AGS/AMA/ASPC/NMA/PCNA/SGIM Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults (2025); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, hypertension, hyperlipidemia and ischemic heart disease monographs (2026) [S]

Evaluation at intake: resting ECG, basic metabolic panel, TSH, HbA1c, lipid panel, one-time lipoprotein(a) and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio; stop and rest, and call the same day for chest discomfort at rest or lasting more than a few minutes, fainting or palpitations; referee only short undercards until the consultation. Guideline: 2025 AHA/ACC/AANP/AAPA/ABC/ACCP/ACPM/AGS/AMA/ASPC/NMA/PCNA/SGIM Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults (2025); 2021 AHA/ACC/ASE/CHEST/SAEM/SCCT/SCMR Guideline for the Evaluation and Diagnosis of Chest Pain (2021); 2026 ACC/AHA/AACVPR/ABC/ACPM/ADA/AGS/APhA/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline on the Management of Dyslipidemia (2026) [S]

Money worries and mood: PHQ-9 and GAD-7 at intake and at six months; generic once-daily medicines at the lowest cost; a social needs screen; brief support and problem-solving at each visit. Guideline: Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults: Screening (2023); Anxiety Disorders in Adults: Screening (2023) [S]
Referral to cardiology, Daniel Achebe-Lindqvist, MD, ordered 1946-05-12 [S]
